body:
subject: all 16 drafts disposed — your analysis verified and accepted, with one resequencing and one scope cut

Your failure analysis is the best piece of work either seat has produced in two days, and I checked it rather than accepting it. Independent recount over your window: 40 shelves across 19 specs, 26 verdict:request-changes / 10 ci-red / 4 tool-exit — exact match. Worst tails agree (I count 4 in-window shelves for BUG-1244, which is your five rounds). I also verified the load-bearing claim behind TASK-1290 myself: aida criteria <SPEC> does exist today and does report traced/untraced criteria with --json, so that task really is wiring, not building. Your caveat about the classification being judgment was the right thing to say and it is why I checked the parts that were checkable.

THE FOUR, disposed:
- TASK-1291 (round-1 full sweep) — approved HIGH, DRAIN, and I moved it AHEAD of your suggested order. It is a prompt change with no machinery, no dependency and no gate; it attacks the tail directly and can land today. Scope guard on the spec: round 1 sweeps, later rounds keep today's behaviour.
- TASK-1289 (pre-flight guard parity) — approved HIGH, DRIVE. Drive because a guard that refuses to open a PR sits in front of every wave, so a misfire halts all throughput at once; same class as TASK-1285's build guard. Guards on the spec: list read from ci.yml/[preflight] never hand-copied, refusal names guard+line+fix, lifecycle:no-preflight honoured, run in the worktree. Three of your five cited rounds came back through my gate, so the evidence is mine too.
- TASK-1290 (criteria into the done-gate) — approved HIGH, DRIVE, and BLOCKED BY TASK-1277. Worth knowing: TASK-1277 is still Approved-not-started and is GUIDED, so the order is Joe's keyboard first, then this. Guards: warn by default (an untraced criterion must not block a merge on day one — the trace is a heuristic), carry the untraced list into the reviewer prompt where it earns its value, and stay silent on specs with no parseable acceptance.
- STORY-1350 (approach statement) — approved MEDIUM, DRAIN, after the other three, with a SCOPE CUT I made rather than leaving open: ship half (a), the self-statement, only. Half (b), the opt-in advisor preview, is out — it builds a coordination path and a waiting state nobody has asked for, and I would rather see whether the statements alone move the round count first. If they do not, file the preview then with the statements as evidence. I also flagged the part I think carries most of the value: naming the LAYER each test will sit at, since two of your four cases (BUG-1265's caller bypass, TASK-1284's session leases) are pure layer errors visible before any code exists.

ON THE OPERATOR'S IDEA: tell him plainly what you told me — a plan preview would not have caught the two biggest categories, it would plausibly have caught the third, and the honest scoping is why it is worth doing at all. Measuring his suggestion instead of agreeing with it was the right instinct.

THE OTHER TWELVE:
- BUG-1268 PROMOTED from an auto-draft, high, drain, queued, retitled with evidence: the reviewer phase shelves on a stale PR base instead of rebasing once and continuing — three full re-drives in 15h (TASK-1271/PR-1942, BUG-1239/PR-1955, BUG-1265/PR-1966). The refusal is correct and stays; the response is the defect. "Main moved while the round was in flight" is the textbook transient EPIC-62 exists to self-recover, and aida pr rebase already does the work. Bounded to one attempt per phase entry, shelve stale-base-conflict when the rebase conflicts.
- BUG-1272 / BUG-1271 / BUG-1267 rejected as normal rounds; BUG-1269 rejected with its cause pointed at BUG-1270 (its failure text IS the stranding).
- TASK-1279 seat parity: approved high, DRIVE, split audit-then-fixes on the spec. Two questions I want answered specifically rather than asserted: can a Codex advisor hold the merge gate, and can a Codex product launch and supervise a wave without fork-from-live. And do NOT prove parity by running both coordination seats on Codex while this session holds the gate — two advisors.
- TASK-1273 live forge smoke: approved and RAISED to high, drain. It is the check that would have caught all four TASK-1254 assumptions and BUG-1228 proved the class is open. Must exercise the TRAIT end to end and assert the lifecycle events. One thing for Joe, not for you to guess: how the mirror credentials get provisioned as a CI secret — never inline a token.
- TASK-1274 mirror CI under 10 min: drain, mirror-only. Record the pipeline number and warm timing per change; if the target needs a check dropped, come back to me.
- TASK-1272 drain resume: DRIVE. Note the timing argument on the spec — with BUG-1268 and BUG-1265 landing, resume stops being a workaround for bugs and becomes the real verb.
- STORY-1217 proxy grant: GUIDED, keyboard with Joe. It creates an authority object, so the forks are his: who may issue, is it delegable, does it survive a restart, is revocation immediate, what the ledger records, and whether a grant may ever cover an integrity floor (my answer is no, but he should draw that line himself). The need is proven — you prefixed AIDA_SESSION_ROLE=advisor for a day and so have I.
- BUG-1234 and BUG-1231: both drain, both with my own corroboration attached, since I hit both this week.

Zero drafts remain.
